headline: NW blows outside — halibut inside, Santa Cruz backside early
body:
The small craft advisory runs through late Thursday night, and the weekend doesn't earn a downgrade offshore: the outer waters from Pt. Sal to Santa Cruz get NW 25–30 kt Saturday with seas building to 8–10 ft, and 25–35 kt Sunday. Inside the east channel it's a different ocean — 5 kn at the harbor, 3.2 ft Saturday and 3.7 ft Sunday — but the western portion still goes NW 20–30.

Fish inside. Saturday is the call: halibut on the Goleta–Carpinteria sand, 3.5 ft, 72.7°F, flat at dawn and only 5 kn SSW gusting 7 by afternoon. Sunday is serviceable at 4 ft and 71°F. For yellowtail, the backside of Santa Cruz holds 70.3°F with 6–7 kn through midday both days; troll the 80-ft line early and be headed home before Saturday's 15 kn gusting 26 fills in late afternoon.

Skip the long runs. Santa Rosa Flats is 24–29 kn, 6.6–7.9 ft, and 63.4°F dropping to 61.8 — cold and unfishable. Osborn at 73.9°F and San Nicolas at 71.9°F aren't worth 68–73 nm in 5–6.5 ft.
